answer: Each epoch, a peer draws one micro-benchmark from a hidden garden of held-out kernel tasks and issues it to a claimed identity with a hard wall-clock deadline of 900 ms; the identity must stream a partial gradient plume as it computes, so its answer carries a live timing trace. Because a clone farm would time-share one GPU across many identities, the verifier stalls each trace against its own deadline: a single shared card serving two clones blows the budget, since the second waits behind the first and its plume arrives 400+ ms late, leaving a telltale echo of the first task's cache state.
